chapters.title: Chapter 4: Second-Order Greeks for Volatility Trading

children.text: The last lesson's table flagged Charm and moved on. It is the reason NSE's weekly Nifty and Bank Nifty expiry days feel different from an ordinary Tuesday even when the index barely moves: near-the-money options bleed delta fast purely from the calendar turning, and a desk that only watches spot for its rehedging cue gets caught flat-footed.

body.text: Charm measures how Delta changes purely from time passing, spot and IV held fixed. It is small and easy to ignore for a 30-day option, and it accelerates sharply for near-the-money strikes as expiry approaches, which is exactly the environment of an NSE weekly expiry day.

markDefs.definition: The change in Delta per unit of calendar time passing, spot and IV held fixed, equal to the change in Theta per unit of spot. Sometimes called Delta decay or Delta bleed.

children.text: is ∂Delta/∂t, calendar time forward, which by the same equality of mixed partials behind Vanna is identical to ∂Theta/∂S. Like Vanna and Volga, its closed form runs through d1 and d2.

body.caption: Charm per year of calendar time, for a call or a put alike, since Delta_put = Delta_call − 1 and the constant −1 has zero time-derivative

body.label: Charm at Chapter 1's 25,700 strike, 30 days out
body.context: Reusing S = 26,500, K = 25,700, IV = 16.8%, T = 30/365, r = 6.5%, with d1 ≈ 0.7714, d2 ≈ 0.7232, φ(d1) ≈ 0.2963 already established: Charm ≈ 0.2963 × (0.7232/0.1644 − 0.065/0.04816) ≈ 0.2963 × 3.050 ≈ 0.904 per year, or ≈ 0.0025 per day. This ITM call's delta drifts up toward 1.0 as expiry nears, since there is less time left for spot to fall back through the strike, and by the same logic the equal-strike OTM put's delta drifts toward 0.

children.text: Why the Effect Depends So Much on Moneyness

The 1/T term in Charm's formula suggests the effect should blow up as expiry nears, but that only happens where φ(d1) stays large enough to matter. A strike sitting clearly ITM or OTM has a small, fading φ(d1) as T shrinks, its outcome is already close to certain, so Charm there stays modest and can even shrink again in the option's final hours. A strike sitting close to the money keeps φ(d1) near its peak the whole way to expiry, so its Charm genuinely accelerates. Hold Nifty's ATM strike fixed and only shrink time to see it.

body.caption: Illustrative ATM Charm, S = K = 26,500, IV held fixed at 13.2%, r = 6.5%, only T changes

body.text: ATM Charm more than quintuples from 30 days to expiry day, while the 25,700 strike's Charm barely moved across the same window in the earlier example. Notice the sign here is negative, not positive: at exactly S = K with a positive risk-free rate, delta sits a little above 0.50, since positive rates give the call a slight built-in advantage that needs time to matter. As that time runs out, delta drifts back down toward exactly 0.50. Chapter 1's IV surface and this chapter's Greeks are the same object seen two ways: a strike's position on the skew determines its σ, which feeds directly into how fast its delta bleeds as expiry nears.

body.caption: Analytic Charm checked against a finite-difference bump in time to expiry, reproducing the ATM 7-day figure from the table above

children.text: A risk reversal or a vol butterfly, the structures from Chapter 2, are never built from options with identical IV. The OTM put leg sits on the higher, put-side skew, the OTM call leg sits on the lower call-side skew, so even at equal delta and equal time to expiry, their σ inputs differ and their Charm values differ correspondingly. A desk planning how much rehedging a multi-leg skew position will need through an expiry week cannot assume one Charm number applies to the whole structure, each leg bleeds delta at its own rate, set by where it sits on the smile as much as by its moneyness.

body.title: Projecting cumulative delta bleed
body.prompt: Using the table above, ATM Charm at 7 days to expiry is −0.0022 per day. If 3 calendar days pass with spot and IV unchanged, what is the approximate cumulative change in delta? (Linear approximation: Charm × number of days)
body.explanation: −0.0022 × 3 = −0.0066. An ATM delta that started at roughly 0.56 would drift to roughly 0.553 over those three days, spot and IV completely unchanged. This is exactly the rehedging need a desk must plan for purely from the calendar, before considering any actual market move.

body.title: Where Charm matters most
body.question: Why does Charm accelerate sharply into expiry for near-the-money strikes specifically, rather than for all strikes equally?
options: Charm only exists for at-the-money options; other strikes have zero Charm
φ(d1) stays large near the money as T shrinks, so the 1/T growth in the formula is not offset, while it fades quickly for clearly ITM or OTM strikes
NSE widens strike intervals for near-the-money options as expiry approaches
Charm is a regulatory margin add-on that only applies to ATM strikes in the final week
body.explanation: Charm's formula combines a term that grows like 1/T with φ(d1). Near the money, φ(d1) stays close to its peak all the way to expiry, so the 1/T growth shows through directly. Away from the money, φ(d1) itself shrinks toward zero as the outcome becomes more certain, capping how large Charm can get. Charm is a genuine Greek, not a margin rule, and every strike has some non-zero Charm.

body.title: Managing a weekly-expiry book
body.scenario: It is the morning of Nifty's weekly expiry. Your book is delta-hedged and holds a meaningful position in ATM and near-ATM strikes, both calls and puts across a couple of nearby strikes straddling spot, alongside further OTM legs from an existing risk reversal. Spot has been essentially flat all morning.
body.prompt: Given what you now know about Charm, why might this book still require active rehedging through the day even though spot has not moved, and which part of the book needs the closest attention?
body.modelAnswer:
1. A flat spot does not mean a flat delta. The ATM and near-ATM legs sit exactly in the regime where Charm is largest and still accelerating hour by hour as the trading day, and the remaining hours to expiry, tick down.
2. The book's net delta will drift purely from this time effect, requiring periodic rehedging trades even with zero directional market movement, essentially the position rehedges itself into a different delta profile as the clock runs, not as spot runs.
3. The further OTM risk reversal legs need comparatively less attention from a pure Charm perspective today, their φ(d1) is smaller and their delta bleed is more modest, consistent with the 25,700-strike example earlier in this lesson.
4. Because the put and call legs on either side of spot sit on different points of the skew, their IVs differ, so even at similar distances from spot their Charm values are not identical, the put-side legs and call-side legs will bleed delta at somewhat different rates through the day.
5. The practical response is to schedule rehedging checks through the day specifically around the ATM and near-ATM strikes, rather than relying purely on a spot-move trigger, since on expiry day the calendar itself, not just the market, is actively moving the book's delta.
6. This is exactly why NSE's high-volume weekly expiry sessions see so much late-day hedging and unwind activity even on days without major news, a large share of it is mechanical delta rebalancing driven by Charm and Gamma accelerating together into the close, not fresh directional views.

cards.definition: ∂Delta/∂t = ∂Theta/∂S. The rate at which Delta changes purely from calendar time passing, spot and IV held fixed. Also called Delta decay or Delta bleed.
Charm accelerates sharply into expiry for near-the-money strikes, where φ(d1) stays large, but stays modest for clearly ITM or OTM strikes, where φ(d1) fades.
Charm is identical for a call and put at the same strike, since Delta_put = Delta_call − 1 and a constant has zero time-derivative.
Different strikes on a smile carry different IV inputs, so even equal-delta legs on opposite sides of the skew bleed delta at different rates, complicating rehedging on a multi-leg skew position.
The practical consequence of Charm on NSE's high-volume weekly expiry days: near-ATM positions require active rehedging purely from time passing, even with spot completely flat.

points: Charm, ∂Delta/∂t = ∂Theta/∂S, measures how Delta bleeds away purely from calendar time passing, spot and IV held fixed, and is identical for a call and put at the same strike.

At Chapter 1's 25,700 strike, 30 days out, Charm is modest, about +0.0025 per day. At the ATM strike, Charm more than quintuples moving from 30 days to expiry day, from about −0.0011 to about −0.0058 per day.

Charm accelerates into expiry specifically for near-the-money strikes, where φ(d1) stays large; strikes clearly away from the money see comparatively little growth as their outcome becomes more certain.

A skewed multi-leg position, a risk reversal or vol butterfly, bleeds delta at different rates on its put-side and call-side legs, since each leg's Charm depends on its own point on the smile, not just its moneyness.

This is the mechanical, non-directional driver behind much of the hedging activity seen on NSE's high-volume weekly Nifty and Bank Nifty expiry days: near-ATM books need active rehedging through the day purely because the calendar is moving, independent of whether spot is.

This completes the second-order Greek toolkit, Vanna for spot-vol cross-sensitivity, Volga for vol convexity, Charm for time-driven delta bleed. The final lesson combines Vanna and Volga into a single, practical smile-consistent pricing adjustment.
